blocking.issue: One runbook command is not exact and fails as written. In RUNBOOK.md step 3 (offline rescoring), the dry-run line `python3 -E -s -B $OPS/rescore_jobs.py submit --export $X --analysis-dir $A --inputs $INPUTS "${RUNS[@]}" --dry-run` leaves out `--out`. rescore_jobs.py marks `--out` as required for both `submit` and `coverage`, so argparse refuses the line (exit 2) before it prints any command. Nothing is submitted, so no harm is done, but the operator meets a failing step and does not get the dry-run preview the runbook promises.
blocking.evidence: I ran it on the scratch export with D59 synthetic run directories. Output: 'rescore_jobs.py submit: error: the following arguments are required: --out', exit=2. The same command with `--out <path> --dry-run` printed the correct sbatch line (--time=08:00:00, metric image 2006c1a9..., Q2M_EXTRA_RO=<run>:/ro/run) and wrote no file. The owner's test test_rescore_submit_dry_run_uses_eight_hours_and_the_metric_image passes `--out`, which is why it did not catch this. Every other runbook command matches its script's argparse: provenance, rules dr0, rescore merge, coverage, costs, run_report, check_identity, first_divergence, glmm write/submit/collect, assemble_s15.
blocking.minimal_fix: Add `--out $A/rescore-jobs.json` to the step-3 dry-run line. With --dry-run the script never writes that file, so the real submit can still create it. Alternatively, make `--out` optional when `--dry-run` is given. Then re-run the dry-run line once.
